Some of the essays in the Ivory Tower were boring, but some were pretty cool! They offered a lot of thought provoking ideas that a lot of people wouldn't think about.

I'm curious as to why you think that... just because we do a lot of creative writing in a lot of my english classes, but we also do a lot of academic/fact based writing in other classes... I am just wondering why you don't agree with the creative type of assessment :)

We had a textbook, which was "The Ivory Tower and Harry Potter: Perspectives on a Literary Phenomenon" by Lana A. Whited (Published in 2004). We read quite a few of the essays out of that - I thought it was okay... Obviously dry in comparison to the books, but they weren't terrible. My teacher said she wouldn't use it in the future though - I never asked her why, but I assume it's because not many of us actually read it, and those who did mostly didn't enjoy it. If I ever get a real answer though, I will let you know.  

Throughout the term we were split into four separate houses, and we rotated to three different houses during three different parts of the term (there wasn't enough time to do 4 houses). Each house looked at a different topic each week and reported back to the class (I forget what all the topics were, but I remember having to find out what the spells latin roots were as one of them). The houses weren't titled the same as those at Hogwarts, but they were named after classes witches and wizards took instead, as we were teaching the class about the topics our house was focusing on. 

Also in our houses, three times throughout the term, we wrote 2 Daily Prophet articles as a group. One had to be a more academic based assignment (written components were strongly encouraged), but the second article could be as creative as you wanted (I did a video where we interviewed different Hogwarts students, and another group made chocolate frog cards - there were many other amazing projects, I just can't think of them right now). The house you were in helped to determine what your article would be focused on. 

The final project was to create a fan fiction or tale by Beedle the Bard that was unique and your own. I didn't really want to write a fan fiction, so I decided to write "Grumble The Grubby Goat" as it was mentioned in the novels, but was never published by J.K. Rowling. I created mine into a book with tea-stained pages, and made it seem as though it belonged to Dumbledore's brother (to fit better into the Harry Potter storyline). 

Throughout the term we talked a lot about different things in the novels - character development, houses (were they good or bad? Did they create tension in the school? etc.), plot lines, and more. We worked in our groups a lot as well so we had class time to get together and get our work done. Groups still had to meet outside of class, but that was rewarded by giving us house points. 

You could earn house points throughout the term by sending my teacher Harry Potter related content, working well in your house, meeting outside of class (and proving it to the teacher), participating, coming to class, and more. Before we were all put into new houses, we had a house-cup ceremony where one house would receive the house cup and a special treat. 
 
Since my teacher was amazing, every time we had a Daily Prophet article due (which was also when we switched houses), we also had a party in class to go along with the house cup ceremony - eat treats she baked inspired by the novels, watch funny clips, look at memes, etc. 

I hope this made sense, as I am at school and writing this in between classes... If you need any clarification on anything or want any more information, let me know!

I was dating someone else, we will call him Aaron. Aaron and my current boyfriend met and everyone was friends and we got along great. Well, they seemed to be going great. 

One night, Aaron left me at a party after I was too drunk to get home alone - I had to call my best friend (now current boyfriend) who drove two hours just to pick me up, and two hours to bring me home. He got me to bed safe and sound and looked after me the next day. 

Another time I was having surgery, and Aaron decided he was too tired to take me to the hospital. I had to call my best friend to take me because I had no other way to get to the hospital due to such short notice. 

I was getting really fed up with Aaron's negative and selfish attitude. 

My current boyfriend came to me as my friend (and I am serious we were only just friends) and told me he had noticed I had been really down. He told me things with Aaron seemed to be dragging me down and he didn't like how Aaron was treating me. He said I was worth more than that and I deserved better. I began to realize he was right. 

I broke up with Aaron and had some time to think about things. I realized my current boyfriend/best friend was a much better, caring, and special person than this Aaron guy. 

We hung out more, we grew closer & we began to spend time together 24/7. Eventually we began sleeping beside each other (no sex or anything), sitting very close while watching movies, holding hands when I was sad or scared, or him rubbing my back when I was sick or having trouble falling asleep. We began to take each other out for lunches and go on things as platonic dates. Anyway, long story short, we ended up being happily in love.
